sec.cmd.suggest_reveal: Read a sealed file in plaintext without unsealing it on disk
sec.cmd.suggest_reveal_out: write an opened copy to this path instead of printing
sec.cmd.suggest_reveal_force: overwrite the --out file if it exists
sec.reveal.terminal_only: reveal runs only in an interactive terminal: here (ACP, server or web UI) the plaintext would leave this machine.
sec.reveal.usage_hint: Open one with /config security reveal <file> (Tab completes the name), or write a copy with --out <path>. The original stays sealed.
sec.reveal.not_found: %q is not a sealed store file.
sec.reveal.list_hint: Run /config security reveal with no file to list them.
sec.reveal.binary: %s is binary (%s); write it to a file with --out <path>.
sec.reveal.header: ── %s (opened in memory; the file on disk stays sealed) ──
sec.reveal.truncated: Showing the first %s of %s; write the whole file with /config security reveal %s --out <path>.
sec.reveal.out_in_root: --out must be outside the state root (%s): a plaintext copy must not sit among the sealed stores.
sec.reveal.out_exists: %s already exists; add --force to overwrite it.
sec.reveal.written_warn: This copy is plaintext: delete it when you are done.
